initial_ruling: Goal credited to Kings goaltender Rogie Vachon after the Islanders' Bryan Trottier pass missed its mark and slid into New York's empty net during a delayed penalty. PA announcer credited Vachon; would have been the first NHL goal credited to a goaltender.
corrected_ruling: Goal credited to Kings forward Vic Venasky, determined to be the last Kings player to touch the puck. Kings won the game 3-0; only player attribution changed.
reason: Kings broadcaster Bob Miller reviewed his play-by-play tape after the period and found no evidence Vachon touched the puck; he alerted the official scorer.
evidence_notes: NHL.com (Kings team site) feature confirms date (Feb. 15, 1977), first-period timing, and postgame correction to Venasky. Exact game clock not stated in the source. Wikipedia's 'List of goalscoring NHL goaltenders' and hockeygoalies.org independently describe the same correction (they describe the review as video review; the NHL.com feature attributes the discovery to the broadcaster's tape).

initial_ruling: Goal credited to Rangers goaltender Bob Froese after Islanders' Brent Sutter's errant pass slid into New York's empty net during a delayed penalty; Froese was announced as only the second NHL goaltender credited with a goal.
corrected_ruling: Goal re-credited to Rangers defenseman David Shaw. The NHL stripped the goal from Froese after review determined Froese never touched the puck (the puck had hit the post). Rangers won 3-1; only player attribution changed.
reason: Videotape review showed the puck hit the goal post, not Froese, so he was not the last Rangers player to touch it. Froese himself told coaches after watching the replay.
evidence_notes: Game date, period and clock (8:59 of the 2nd) from The Washington Post (Nov. 30, 1987). The New York Times (Dec. 10, 1987) reports 'Last Friday, the N.H.L. stripped Bob Froese of the goal', placing the league correction around Dec. 4, 1987 — several days after the game. No NHL.com document found; flagged for that reason.

initial_ruling: Buffalo's goal (Robert Reichel own goal into the empty net) was announced with Dmitri Kalinin as the scorer during the Sabres' 6-4 win over Toronto.
corrected_ruling: Goal credited to Sabres goaltender Mika Noronen, the last Buffalo player to touch the puck before Reichel put it into his own net. Noronen learned of the correction about 10 minutes after the game ended.
reason: Postgame scoring review determined Noronen, not Kalinin, was the last Sabres player to touch the puck.
evidence_notes: NHL.com article (Dec. 5, 2007) documents the correction, including Noronen's quote. Period and clock are not stated in the source and are left null rather than assumed.

initial_ruling: P.K. Subban goal on the ice at 7:13 of the first period (Stanley Cup Final Game 1) — what would have been Nashville's first goal of the Final.
corrected_ruling: No goal. Pittsburgh coach Mike Sullivan challenged for offside; review determined Filip Forsberg preceded the puck into the zone without possession. First coach's challenge in Stanley Cup Final history. Pittsburgh went on to win 5-3.
reason: Offside on the zone entry preceding the goal (Rule 78.7 offside challenge).
evidence_notes: No NHL.com Situation Room post located for this 2017 review (the league's per-review posts came later). Verified via ESPN game coverage and AP reporting of the league's written explanation. Review took about four minutes.

initial_ruling: Mikko Rantanen goal on the ice at 17:26 of the third period, which would have tied the game 4-4.
corrected_ruling: Call overturned on St. Louis offside challenge (Sven Andrighetto ruled offside) — no goal. The next day the NHL issued a statement admitting the review itself should never have happened: the puck had cleared the zone, resetting the entry, so under Rule 78.7 'the goal should have counted'. The result was not changed.
reason: Offside challenge upheld by the Situation Room in error. Rule 78.7 only permits offside review of the zone entry immediately preceding the goal; the earlier offside was nullified when the puck left the zone.
evidence_notes: Official NHL statement dated Oct. 20, 2017. St. Louis won 4-3; had the goal counted, Colorado would have tied the game late and St. Louis would have taken a minor penalty for the failed challenge.

initial_ruling: Jesperi Kotkaniemi goal on the ice at 15:29 of the second period; an initial video review (puck crossing the line) upheld it as a goal, cutting Toronto's lead to 4-3.
corrected_ruling: No goal after a second review. Toronto challenged for goaltender interference; video review determined Kotkaniemi pushed Frederik Andersen's pad, causing the puck to enter the net (Rule 69.7). Toronto won 5-3.
reason: Goaltender interference found on the second review after the goal had already survived the first review — a same-game double reversal.
evidence_notes: Official NHL.com Situation Room post (dated Feb. 21, 2021) documents the challenge result and rule citation; game date and double-review sequence corroborated by theScore and Montreal Gazette coverage.

initial_ruling: Victor Olofsson goal on the ice with 57 seconds left in the third period (deflection off goalie Alexandar Georgiev and defenseman Patrik Nemeth) that would have tied the game 2-2.
corrected_ruling: No goal: Situation Room-initiated review reversed the call for offside (Rasmus Dahlin tag-up). Two days later the NHL admitted the reversal was wrong: replay could not definitively determine Olofsson touched the puck before Dahlin tagged up, so league policy required staying with the original 'good goal' call. The result was not changed; the Rangers won 2-1.
reason: Offside review overturned the goal although replay was inconclusive; the NHL later stated 'The original call on the ice, good goal, should have stood.'
evidence_notes: Official NHL.com article (Dec. 12, 2021) quoting NHL senior EVP Colin Campbell's statement. Game played Friday Dec. 10, 2021.

initial_ruling: Aleksander Barkov goal on the ice roughly 10 seconds after Adam Henrique's 2-0 goal early in the second period of Stanley Cup Final Game 6.
corrected_ruling: No goal. Edmonton challenged for offside; video review determined Sam Reinhart preceded the puck into the offensive zone. Clock reset to 19:09 (0:51 elapsed). Edmonton preserved a 2-0 lead and won 5-1 to force a Game 7.
reason: Offside on the zone entry preceding the goal (Rule 38.9). Panthers coach Paul Maurice publicly disputed the conclusiveness of the review.
evidence_notes: Official NHL.com Situation Room post names the teams, period and rule but not the scorer; scorer (Barkov) and game context verified via ESPN, USA Today and Wikipedia's 2024 Stanley Cup Final summary.

initial_ruling: Mikko Rantanen power-play goal on the ice at 9:11 of the second period (made it 4-2 Colorado).
corrected_ruling: Goal confirmed after a double review. Seattle challenged for offside (Artturi Lehkonen); the referee first announced the goal disallowed, then the Situation Room re-opened the review: Seattle's Yanni Gourde had played the puck back into his own zone, which nullifies offside under Rule 83.1. Final: call on the ice upheld — goal Colorado; Seattle assessed a minor penalty for an unsuccessful challenge. Colorado won 6-3.
reason: Rule 83.1 exception: offside is ignored when a defending player plays the puck back into his own zone while an opponent is in the zone.
evidence_notes: Official NHL.com post gives the final outcome ('Call on the ice is upheld – Goal Colorado', Rule 83.1, unsuccessful-challenge penalty). The intermediate 'no goal' announcement before the second review is documented by Scouting The Refs and The Hockey Beast; the NHL post itself does not describe that intermediate step.
